items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept concealed?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The context is the mortal world among base people
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching properly be transmitted?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is numbered fifth
The section is a chapter
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter in the text from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of Kaula been understood?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Understanding arose by that lord's grace
What is known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: The speaker has understood the determination of Kaula through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have understood the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and how should this be explained?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
The speaker requests a complete explanation
items.inference: The speaker asks to be told fully into what the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The reality in question is defined as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and śakti?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
It is characterized as power and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: The precise sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is situated within beings
Its scope includes all living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the given form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is ascribed to the soul upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
The subject is then designated
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes through an unbroken lineage
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is received orally in the ear through traditional succession.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing alone is emphasized
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even mere heard knowledge has a significant effect for the addressed listener.
uncertainties: The main consequence is completed in the following verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is undertaken for six months
The practitioner engages in the prescribed discipline
The state attained is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The exact sense of kāṣāyaṃ in this context is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits result from the prescribed practice for the practitioner?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with yogis is achieved
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
A teaching has been told to her
The teaching concerns the practice of the soul
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: What qualities must a worthy recipient possess to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The phrase sarva+bhāva+upapannasya admits multiple interpretations.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one endowed with all states and of firm resolve.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is not to be given
It is the essence of Kaula teaching
It originates from the yoginīs
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of sambhavam is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
A change is asserted now
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: The body, once struck by ignorance, is now claimed to be pure.
uncertainties: deham appears in accusative form but functions as subject here.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time is now sought?
premises: The speaker now wishes to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired knowledge is the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: The speaker seeks to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is no doubt in the teaching
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching assures without doubt that death can be destroyed.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you without doubt how death is destroyed.

items.question: What condition afflicts even the wise at the source of nectar?
premises: The location is the tip of nectar
There is burning by the essence of juice
Even a wise person is affected
items.inference: Even the wise may experience burning at the source of nectar.
uncertainties: The physiological referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are esoteric.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one is burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: How should the practitioner draw in the vital air during this technique?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner prepares the position
The vital air should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly draw in the vital air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Having positioned at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the air.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is attained through this accomplished practice?
premises: The body may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
Poison does not enter the practitioner's body
items.inference: Through this practice, poison does not enter the body even if bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
